title: Paved Roads: Starting an Internal Developer Platform
abstract: Explains how a small platform team can build paved roads, meaning opinionated templates and self-service workflows, so application developers ship without filing tickets. Covers picking the first three golden paths and measuring whether they actually save time.
speaker: Priya Venkataraman (Helix Ridge Software)

title: Tracing One Click Through Forty Microservices
abstract: A walkthrough of distributed tracing for systems where a single user click fans out into dozens of service calls. The talk shows how to propagate context, sample intelligently, and turn trace timelines into plain answers about where latency comes from.
speaker: Mateus Okonkwo-Reyes (Lumen Harbor Analytics)

title: Workload Identity Without Static Secrets
abstract: Long-lived API keys and passwords stored in config files remain a leading cause of cloud breaches. This session covers short-lived workload identities, token exchange between clusters and clouds, and how to retire secrets without breaking deployments.
speaker: Hanne Vestergaard (Fjordline Cyber)

title: Onboarding a New Engineer to Production in One Afternoon
abstract: A practical guide to making laptop-to-cluster setup fast, using devcontainers, seeded test data, and one-command local environments. Attendees leave with a checklist for trimming onboarding friction and a list of the blockers that show up most often.
speaker: Dara Oyelaran-Smith (Cobalt Tern Labs)

title: Showback Dashboards Engineers Actually Open
abstract: Cloud cost reports fail when only finance can see them. This talk shows how to publish per-team spend views inside tools engineers already use, and how to connect cost to deployments without punishing experimentation.
speaker: Tomasz Winterbourne (Ledgerfield Cloud)

title: Scheduling GPU Inference Without Burning the Cluster
abstract: GPUs are expensive and easy to waste, so inference workloads need careful bin packing, time slicing, and autoscaling driven by queue depth rather than CPU. The session compares device plugins, multi-instance GPU partitioning, and warm pools for large language model serving.
speaker: Ines Carvalho-Mbeki (Vantablue Compute)

title: Ambient Service Mesh in Production: A Year of Lessons
abstract: Sidecar-free service meshes promise lower overhead and simpler upgrades, but migration hides sharp edges around mutual TLS, layer 7 policy, and waypoint proxies. This session shares incident reports, measured latency numbers, and a rollback plan that worked.
speaker: Gunnar Halvorsen-Pike (Driftwood Networks)

title: Stateful Workloads on Ephemeral Nodes
abstract: Databases and message queues still need durable disks even when the nodes underneath are replaced constantly. This talk explains volume snapshots, topology-aware provisioning, and how to test node drains before a disk-bound pod gets stuck.
speaker: Ruth Abernathy-Chen (Quarry Block Systems)

title: Running Small Services at the Edge Without a Data Center
abstract: Edge computing means running code close to users on small devices, cell-site servers, or regional points of presence. This introductory session explains where latency really matters, how to keep edge nodes patched, and what to do when a connection drops for hours.
speaker: Kofi Mensah-Lindqvist (Tidewater Edge)

title: Mentoring Your First Kubernetes Contributor
abstract: Open source projects depend on newcomers who stick around, but most mentoring is informal and inconsistent. This talk offers a simple structure for good-first-issue triage, review etiquette, and spotting contributors who want to grow into maintainers.
speaker: Lucia Ferreira-Odum (Open Harvest Foundation)

title: Logs, Metrics, Traces: Choosing What to Collect First
abstract: Teams often collect everything and understand nothing. This session gives a plain-language map of logs, metrics, and traces, with a decision guide for starting small and adding signals when a question keeps going unanswered.
speaker: Asha Kiplagat-Doyle (Brightwater Telemetry)

title: Policy as Code for Admission Control
abstract: Admission controllers and policy engines let teams reject insecure manifests before they reach a cluster. The talk compares Rego-based and CEL-based policies, shows how to roll out enforcement in audit mode first, and covers handling exceptions without weakening guardrails.
speaker: Elias Brandt-Nakamura (Keystone Gate Security)

title: Multi-Tenant Clusters Versus Cluster Sprawl
abstract: Should each team get a cluster, a namespace, or a virtual cluster? This session analyzes the isolation, cost, and operations trade-offs, including noisy neighbor problems, quota design, and how to change tenancy models without downtime.
speaker: Shu-Fen Adeyemi-Berg (Northstar Infra)

title: DNS Failures Are Never Just DNS
abstract: Most intermittent production errors blamed on DNS actually come from connection pooling, resolver search-path settings, or caching. This talk walks through real debugging sessions and shows the tools that separate a name lookup problem from a network path problem.
speaker: Callum Ruiz-Haddad (Pinecrest Connect)

title: Preview Environments for Every Pull Request
abstract: Temporary environments let reviewers click through a change before it merges, but they quietly raise cost and complexity. The session covers namespace-per-branch patterns, data seeding, automated teardown, and budget guardrails.
speaker: Nadia Solheim-Ware (Mosaic Build Co)

title: Over-the-Air Updates for a Thousand Kiosks
abstract: Pushing firmware and container updates to devices behind flaky cellular links requires staged rollouts, delta downloads, and automatic rollback. This session describes how one retailer updated fifteen hundred kiosks without a single store going dark.
speaker: Rafael Ibarra-Thorne (Sundial Retail Tech)

title: Training Pipelines With Checkpoint Recovery on Spot Capacity
abstract: Spot and preemptible instances cut training costs dramatically, but interrupted jobs waste hours of GPU time. This talk covers checkpoint frequency, distributed training resilience, and queue design that keeps experiments moving when capacity disappears.
speaker: Wren Okafor-Lindgren (Halcyon Data Forge)

title: Unit Economics for Kubernetes Workloads
abstract: Total cloud spend says little about product health, so teams need cost per request, cost per active user, or cost per transaction. This session shows how to derive these numbers from cluster telemetry and how to present them to product leaders.
speaker: Benedikt Asante-Vale (Meridian Ledger)

title: Running a Meetup That People Come Back To
abstract: Local cloud-native meetups survive on volunteer energy and a few reliable habits. This talk shares practical advice on venues, finding speakers, inclusive scheduling, and keeping attendance steady over a full year.
speaker: Ama Boateng-Quill (Lantern Cloud Users Group)

title: Object Storage 101 for Container Apps
abstract: Object storage holds uploads, backups, and build artifacts, but its consistency rules and access patterns differ from disks. This introduction covers buckets, lifecycle policies, presigned URLs, and simple ways to keep data durable without overspending.
speaker: Oleksandr Mirza-Fielding (Cedarlight Storage)

title: Alert Fatigue: Paging Rules That Respect Sleep
abstract: Pagers that fire at 3 a.m. for minor issues burn out on-call engineers and teach teams to ignore alerts. This session covers symptom-based alerting, SLO burn rates, and how to review and retire noisy rules every quarter.
speaker: Maren Lindqvist-Oduya (Sentinel Orbit)

title: Container Image Hygiene in Plain Language
abstract: Container images carry operating system packages, libraries, and build tools that attackers can exploit. This beginner session explains base image selection, minimal images, software bills of materials, and how to scan without drowning in false positives.
speaker: Jaxon Pemberton-Ayala (Harborlight Trust)

title: Building an Internal Catalog Developers Trust
abstract: A service catalog helps engineers find owners, docs, and dependencies, but stale entries erode trust fast. The talk shows how to discover services automatically, assign ownership through code, and make the catalog the default starting point during incidents.
speaker: Esther Malik-Harmon (Crescent Platform Labs)

title: What Is Model Serving and Why Does It Break?
abstract: Serving a machine learning model means exposing a prediction endpoint that stays fast under load and can be updated safely. This plain-language introduction covers batching, versioned rollouts, and why a model that works in a notebook can fail in production.
speaker: Teodor Nakashima-Vale (Pale Juniper AI)

title: Code Review Checklists Developers Don't Resent
abstract: Review checklists can speed up feedback or become bureaucratic punishment. This talk shares a short set of questions for reviewers and authors that catch operational risks, plus how to phase the checklist out as the team matures.
speaker: Simone Achterberg-Lee (Tallgrass Engineering)

title: Ingress, Gateways, and the Path a Packet Takes
abstract: Traffic enters a cluster through load balancers, ingress controllers, and newer Gateway API resources, and each hop adds its own rules. This beginner session traces the full path from a browser to a pod and explains which settings matter most.
speaker: Kiran Desmond-Osei (Lattice Routing Group)

title: Runtime Threat Detection With eBPF Sensors
abstract: Kernel-level sensors can notice a process spawning a shell or reading files it should never touch, even when image scanning missed the problem. The session explains event pipelines, tuning to cut false positives, and how to test detection rules with simulated attacks.
speaker: Ingrid Solberg-Marsh (Rampart Sentinel)

title: Replicating Petabytes Across Regions Without Losing Sleep
abstract: Cross-region replication for large datasets involves bandwidth budgets, conflict resolution, and recovery time targets that look good on slides but break during real outages. This talk shares measured failover drills and the replication layout that survived them.
speaker: Yusuf Alcantara-Brook (Granite Vault Systems)

title: WebAssembly at the Edge: Startup Times and Trade-offs
abstract: WebAssembly modules can start in microseconds and run in sandboxes at the edge, but language support and system calls still limit what fits. This session benchmarks cold starts, compares runtimes, and shows which workloads benefit most.
speaker: Hyejin Park-Dunmore (Lighthouse Runtime)

title: Writing Cloud-Native Content Non-Experts Can Follow
abstract: Technical documentation and conference talks often assume knowledge that newcomers lack. This session covers analogies, glossaries, and structured explanations that help readers and listeners follow complex systems without losing accuracy.
speaker: Farid Nazari-Holt (Plainspoken Labs)

title: Commitment Discounts Without Regret
abstract: Reserved instances and savings plans lower unit costs but lock in capacity that may not fit next quarter. The talk models commitment coverage, forecasting error, and how to structure purchases so engineering flexibility survives budget reviews.
speaker: Lorna Keyes-Oyelowo (Summit Ledger Advisors)

title: Continuous Profiling in Production at Low Overhead
abstract: Sampling CPU and memory profiles continuously reveals performance regressions that synthetic benchmarks miss. This session explains overhead budgets, symbol management, and how to compare flame graphs across releases without drowning in noise.
speaker: Rahul Vashisht-Ogunleye (Quartz Lantern)

title: Feature Flags Without Permanent Technical Debt
abstract: Feature flags speed up releases, but abandoned flags leave dead branches nobody dares to delete. This session shows lifecycle rules, ownership metadata, and automated cleanup jobs that keep flag sprawl under control.
speaker: Marisol Ekwueme-Hart (Vantage Loop Software)

title: Platform Teams Are Product Teams: A Starter Guide
abstract: Platform teams fail when they act as ticket queues instead of products with users, roadmaps, and feedback loops. This introduction explains basic product thinking, interview techniques for internal customers, and how to set adoption goals.
speaker: Gideon Ashworth-Riley (Pinecone Harbor Tech)

title: Egress Control for Clusters That Must Reach the Outside World
abstract: Outbound traffic from workloads is a common route for data theft and surprise bills. This talk covers egress gateways, domain-based allowlists, NAT design, and how to debug blocked calls without asking for broad exceptions.
speaker: Thandiwe Morrow-Espinal (Bluestem Network Co)

title: Your First Edge Device Fleet
abstract: Managing a few dozen connected devices differs from managing a data center: devices reboot, change networks, and need trusted identities. This beginner walkthrough covers device enrollment, certificate rotation, and remote diagnostics.
speaker: Otto Wenzel-Quaye (Hillfort Devices)

title: Vector Search Infrastructure for Semantic Retrieval
abstract: Semantic search finds documents by meaning rather than exact words, which requires embedding pipelines, approximate nearest neighbor indexes, and careful refresh schedules. This session explains how to host vector databases on Kubernetes and measure recall against latency.
speaker: Noor Hadzic-Benning (Sable Index Labs)

title: Securing the Software Supply Chain From Commit to Cluster
abstract: Attackers increasingly compromise build pipelines and dependencies instead of production systems. This talk covers signed commits, provenance attestations, and admission checks that verify who built an artifact and whether it came from an approved source.
speaker: Felix Adubato-Kroll (Ironbark Assurance)

title: Accessible Conference Talks: A Checklist for Speakers
abstract: Talks become inaccessible when slides lack alt text, videos lack captions, or the room has no step-free route. This short session gives speakers a checklist covering captions, sign language interpretation, and quiet spaces for attendees who need them.
speaker: Blessing Oketunde-Carr (Common Ground Events)

title: Backup Restores You Have Actually Tested
abstract: Backups are only useful if restores work under pressure, but many teams never rehearse them. This session covers restore drills, automated backup verification jobs, and metrics that prove recovery time objectives are realistic.
speaker: Camille Renaud-Quist (Rivermark Data)

title: Dashboards That Answer Questions Instead of Decorating Walls
abstract: A dashboard should help someone decide something within seconds, yet many panels show numbers nobody uses. This beginner talk covers choosing the questions first, using consistent time windows, and pruning panels that never change a decision.
speaker: Julian Ekstrom-Pham (Lumen Harbor Analytics)

title: Infrastructure Modules Versus Copy-Paste Templates
abstract: Reusable Terraform or Pulumi modules reduce drift, but poorly versioned modules slow everyone down. The talk compares module registries, semantic versioning rules, and how to upgrade a fleet of stacks safely.
speaker: Yvonne Castellano-Brisk (Keel and Anvil Systems)

title: Confidential Computing for Sensitive Workloads
abstract: Trusted execution environments keep data encrypted while it is in use, which matters for health, finance, and government workloads. This session explains attestation, enclave-enabled node pools, and the performance costs teams should expect.
speaker: Anatoly Brennan-Osei (Velvet Enclave Labs)

title: IPv6 in Clusters: Is It Time?
abstract: IPv6 addresses are plentiful, but dual-stack clusters still raise questions about pod addressing, service endpoints, and legacy integrations. This quick introduction explains where IPv6 is ready today and where it still causes friction.
speaker: Halima Sorensen-Ndiaye (Northwind Carrier Services)

title: Cloud Bills Explained for Non-Finance Engineers
abstract: Invoices list line items with confusing names like egress, requests, and amortized commitments. This plain-language session decodes common cloud bill terms and shows which charges engineers can influence this week.
speaker: Pablo Anand-Rourke (Ledgerfield Cloud)

title: Terminal Tools That Make Kubernetes Less Scary
abstract: Command-line helpers can display cluster state, switch contexts safely, and explain errors in plain language. This beginner demo shows a handful of tools and shell aliases that remove common stumbling blocks.
speaker: Rosalind Okonedo-Winters (Greenfold Tooling)

title: Evaluating LLM Agents in Production Clusters
abstract: Autonomous language model agents call tools, retry failures, and sometimes loop forever, which makes their behavior hard to test. This talk covers evaluation harnesses, guardrails, budget limits, and tracing agent decisions for postmortems.
speaker: Sebastian Quirke-Mori (Falcon Reasoning)

title: Consistency Across Disconnected Edge Sites
abstract: Edge sites lose connectivity for hours, yet their data must eventually reconcile with the core. The talk explains conflict-free replicated data types, local write queues, and how to simulate network partitions in staging.
speaker: Nomvula Sithole-Gray (Ridgeline Telecom Edge)

title: Developer Portals With Real Golden Paths
abstract: Portal projects often stall because they list links rather than solving tasks. This session shows how to connect scaffolding, pipelines, and documentation into one guided flow that a new team can finish in a single sitting.
speaker: Beatriz Villanueva-Hale (Rooftop Engineering)

title: Open Source Governance When a Project Outgrows Its Founders
abstract: Maintainer burnout and unclear decision rules put many successful projects at risk. This talk covers charters, steering committees, release roles, and transparent handoffs that keep contributors engaged.
speaker: Kwame Abiodun-Hart (Open Harvest Foundation)

title: Scaling Connection Tables for High-Churn Microservices
abstract: High request churn exhausts connection tracking tables and causes packet drops that look like application bugs. This advanced session covers kernel tuning, connection reuse, and load tests that reproduce the churn before customers do.
speaker: Ilse Varga-Thornbury (Pinecrest Connect)

title: Tiered Storage for Machine Learning Datasets
abstract: Training datasets grow faster than budgets, so teams need tiered storage that moves cold shards to cheaper media without slowing active jobs. The session compares caching layers, prefetching, and lifecycle rules built for data scientists.
speaker: Dmitri Holloway-Ndlovu (Quarry Block Systems)

title: Platform Engineering Anti-Patterns to Avoid This Year
abstract: Common mistakes include building portals no one uses, mandating tools without support, and hiding costs from product teams. This beginner talk lists the patterns, explains why they happen, and offers simpler alternatives.
speaker: Maeve Kowalczyk-Ibekwe (Northstar Infra)

title: Phishing-Resistant Sign-In for Engineers
abstract: Passwords and one-time codes can be stolen through phishing, while hardware security keys and passkeys resist it. This beginner session explains how to roll out phishing-resistant sign-in to engineers and handle lost devices calmly.
speaker: Gareth Puleo-Ansah (Harborlight Trust)

title: Correlating Logs With Traces Without Vendor Lock-In
abstract: Engineers want logs and traces linked by a shared identifier, but proprietary agents make switching tools painful. This talk shows how OpenTelemetry conventions, consistent resource attributes, and standard exporters keep telemetry portable.
speaker: Hana Ogbonna-Frost (Brightwater Telemetry)

title: Feature Stores and Online Inference Latency
abstract: Real-time models need features computed from fresh data within milliseconds, which strains stores designed for nightly batch jobs. This session covers online feature serving, freshness trade-offs, and monitoring for training-serving skew.
speaker: Yiannis Marchetti-Bell (Pale Juniper AI)

title: Building a Language Server for Internal Config Files
abstract: Teams often write YAML or HCL configuration by hand and only learn about mistakes after deployment. This advanced session shows how to build a language server that gives editors autocomplete, validation, and quick fixes for internal schemas.
speaker: Oluwaseun Fenwick-Abara (Rooftop Engineering)

title: Secure Remote Access to Field Equipment
abstract: Field technicians need to reach devices in remote locations without exposing them to the open internet. This talk covers zero-trust tunnels, short-lived credentials, session recording, and how to support intermittent connections.
speaker: Ingeborg Maddox-Feld (Tidewater Edge)

title: Forecasting Cloud Spend Through a Product Launch
abstract: Launches create sudden traffic spikes that make budgets look wrong overnight. The session shows scenario modeling, guardrail alerts, and how to communicate forecast ranges so finance and engineering agree on a plan.
speaker: Ravi Chandrasekar-Owens (Summit Ledger Advisors)

title: Closing Circle: Where Cloud-Native Goes Next
abstract: A wrap-up conversation about what changed in the community this year, what to learn next, and how newcomers can get involved. It also introduces volunteer roles and the local chapters that welcome first-time speakers.
speaker: Lila Matsuda-Greene (Common Ground Events)
